steps.does: Shows a TradingView overlay chart of many AI-trade and semiconductor stocks and leveraged ETFs, normalised to percent change since the June top, with a colour-coded legend of percent declines, and reads the declines off one by one.
steps.why: To show that stocks already crashed are now seeing capitulation selling, i.e. panic rather than an orderly market.
data: Percent decline since June top per stock (SpaceX -15%, AMD -18%, Avago -19%, TSM -25%, Nvidia -30%+, Oracle -32%, Micron about -50%, Caterpillar -51%, Marvell -55%, CoreWeave -59%, Nebius -67%, Sandisk -72%, Iren -74%)
steps.conclusion: Already-obliterated stocks falling double digits again signals pure capitulation, with leverage being unwound.

steps.does: States forward P/E of the crashed semiconductor names to argue valuations are on the floor and there is no fundamental case for the crash yet; no screen shown for these figures.
steps.why: To separate fear-driven selling from a real fundamental deterioration.
data: Hyperscaler CapEx still guided up for 2027
steps.conclusion: Fundamentals still strong for one to several years; the selloff is fear on fear.

rules.text: Run a bear, base and bull case on each company and understand its risk profile before buying a crash.
A major correction is usually not over until even resilient names like Apple take a 10-15% hit.

steps.does: Searches QQQ in TradingView and views a plain line chart of QQQ since its October high, noting the percent decline.
steps.why: To see how deep the Nasdaq-100 pullback is before reacting to commentators.
steps.conclusion: QQQ is roughly 18% off its highs.

steps.does: Plays YouTube clips of CNBC interviews with Tom Lee, Ed Yardeni and Dan Ives, pausing to react (for example noting Anthropic is also crashing, and that commodities are crashing).
steps.why: To gather Wall Street views on whether the tech correction is healthy and offer a counterview.
data: Tom Lee: healthy correction, comparing to Cisco in 1997
Ed Yardeni: AI trade alive and well
Dan Ives: dark period for tech
steps.conclusion: Creator treats the commentary as context and focuses on buying the dip over years.

steps.does: Switches the TradingView right-hand watchlist to his own holdings and reads each stock's day change, naming which are green or down only 1-2% (CRM, Google, Estee Lauder, On, AmEx, Wynn, RH, Nike).
steps.why: To show which of his holdings are holding up while the AI trade is crashing.
data: CRM green; Estee Lauder, On, AmEx about -1%; Wynn, RH, Nike about -2%
steps.conclusion: Defensive and previously crashed holdings are holding up; usually everything gets hit by the end of a correction.
